A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same WonderPlay research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-B are readable and support a reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original results from a 15-scene benchmark, a 200-participant user study, qualitative experiments, and the ablations and staged evaluation in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and user-study results in Tables 1-2, qualitative experiments, and Appendix A's ablation and staged-evaluation results.

M1.justification: The scene representation, physics solvers, flow/RGB conditioning, spatially varying responsibility, and photometric scene refinement are unchanged. Solver descriptions are moved and merged into Appendix B.4 rather than introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 15 scenes comprising seven real photos and eight synthetic images, with unchanged material and action coverage. The four-stage evaluation and the scenarios illustrated in Figures 5-6 are also retained.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain PhysGen, PhysGaussian, CogVideoX-I2V, and Tora. The staged comparison in Figure S2 retains its original comparator subset, PhysGen and PhysGaussian.

E3.justification: Metrics, scene composition, baseline adaptations, and the user-study protocol of 200 participants evaluating ten scenes each remain unchanged. The 960 simulation steps, 49-frame output, 480-by-720 resolution, and 25-step DDIM sampling are retained; some settings move to Appendix B.1.

E4.justification: Figures 7-8 and Table S1 retain the coarse-simulation, missing-RGB, and missing-flow ablations and the same diffusion-parameter sensitivity results. Appendix A's staged complexity analysis is unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same average and point-estimate reporting. Neither adds repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 and S1 and the curves in Figure S2 retain the same results. For example, WonderPlay's Table 2 imaging and physical-realism scores remain 0.695 and 0.700. Qualitative result panels are unchanged despite shortened descriptions.

T1.justification: Equations 1-5, the scene and object definitions, the photometric objective, and the homogeneous-material assumption are preserved. Relocating solver explanations adds no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: single-image action-conditioned dynamic 3D generation across diverse materials, a hybrid physics/video simulator, and superior visual quality and physical plausibility relative to the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning incomplete reconstruction, simulator limitations, video hallucination, background responsibility, and diffusion-parameter tradeoffs remain. Shortened narration of Figures 5-6 does not revise the substantive interpretations or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: The new Appendix B.1-B.2 headings contain implementation and background-reconstruction details already present in v1's main text. Solver details, Table S2 defaults, surfel-to-particle mapping, the project link, and the promised future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 78 cited works and substantive related-work comparisons are retained, including positioning against PhysMotion and controllable video generation. Reference changes concern citation locations rather than added literature or revised novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 moves background reconstruction, solver descriptions, and generation settings into reorganized Appendix B subsections, trims example narration, and expands funding acknowledgments. These are bounded editorial changes; most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are repositioned, several captions gain bold emphasis, and Table S2 moves onto a largely empty final page. Figure content, plot designs, and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 mainly condenses the main text and consolidates existing technical material in Appendix B while preserving the methods, evidence, and claims. Shorter exposition brings limited editorial benefits, alongside trimmed example explanations and duplicated material-estimation prose in B.4. Overall paper quality remains essentially unchanged.
